KEY MESSAGE 1...Our tricky forecast across the area today 
continues as a complex low pressure system noted by a surface 
low well to the northeast of Cape Hatteras with its associated 
front stretching SW'wards into a second area of low pressure 
noted off the Carolina coast moves NE'wards while a mid level 
shortwave noted across inland North Carolina also moves 
NE'wards this afternoon. Additional mesoscale lows have also 
developed along this front offshore as well which can be seen 
via radar imagery with the general track of this activity 
pushing NE'wards. This has brought light to moderate showers 
across ENC this afternoon with this activity continuing NE 
'wards over the next few hours.

Overall the forecast has not changed much as the broad mid 
level shortwave currently across inland North Carolina is 
rounding the base of a negatively tilted trough and will push
off to the northeast tonight. At the surface, broad and complex 
low pressure system also pushes NE'wards away from the Carolinas 
following the mid level shortwave. Given the broad nature of 
the mid level energy, light showers could hang around ENC into 
late tonight before precip ends from SW to NE. Behind the shower
activity there is a chance for some patchy fog to develop as 
skies begin to clear behind the departing low, winds remain 
light, and ample low level moisture will be in place. As a 
result have kept patchy fog is forecast for much of ENC with 
development possible after midnight.

Ongoing dangerous surf continues across our coastal areas with
local buoy's showing widespread 6-9 ft seas across our coastal
waters. Seas are forecast to gradually lower as the 
aforementioned complex low pressure system departs with the 
ongoing high surf advisory forecast to end by 1AM tonight 
across all coastal areas. Even with the high surf and elevated 
tide levels today we did not see much in the way of water level 
rises so coastal flooding is no longer expected. Otherwise 
0.1-0.25 inches of precip is expected with the leftover shower 
activity today before we dry out tonight. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...We will continue to see increasing water levels
over the next few days as a result of the ongoing King Tide 
Cycle which will continue through the week, peaking during the 
middle of the week. This higher than normal astronomical tide 
cycle is slightly stronger than the one that occurred the last 
week of OCT. The tide levels may be exacerbated by a strong 
front and potentially significant coastal storm which is 
forecast to impact the area starting Tuesday and peaking 
Wed/Thurs.

We will see a cold front drop SE'wards across ENC Mon night into
Tue morning eventually stalling offshore with a rather strong 
high pressure system settling in across the Northeastern CONUS.
As a matter of fact this high pressure will be anonymously 
strong in nature which will act to tighten the pressure 
gradient bringing rather gusty N-NE'rly winds to the area with 
widespread 20-35 mph wind gusts noted for much of the day Tue. 
The King tide cycle will be approaching its peak Tue/Wed which 
could act to pile up water especially soundside in the Pamlico 
sound and in the Neuse River and adjacent areas. This 
combination could lead to some minor water level rises on Tue 
across both soundside and ocean side locations across the OBX 
and near the Neuse River. 

Another stronger low pressure system is expected to impact the 
area Wednesday into Thursday. While there is still some
uncertainty with the exact strength and track of this low there
is increasing confidence for a potentially significant coastal
storm impacting the area Wed onto Thurs bringing strong NE-E 
winds, dangerous surf and hazardous marine conditions. It is 
becoming increasingly likely that most tidal locations across 
ENC should expect elevated water levels with at least minor to 
moderate impacts with the potential for more significant impacts
across the more vulnerable locations given he expected strength
and duration of the winds. Interests along the coast should 
watch the forecast closely over the next few days for the 
potential for greater impacts, especially as it has to potential
to impact holiday travel.

KEY MESSAGE 3...
Yet another somewhat complex forecast is setting up across the 
area that looks to impact the holiday this week. In the upper 
levels a rather potent sub-tropical jet will remain in place 
though much of the week. An upper level trough currently noted 
along the west coast will track E'wards into the Plains as it 
rides along the aforementioned sub-tropical jet, while further 
to the north an upper level low will begin to dive SE'wards from
